newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Singaporeans arrested in biggest Indonesia drug haul.
newsitem.headline: Singaporeans arrested in biggest Indonesia drug haul.

text.p: Indonesian customs officers at Jakarta's Sukarno-Hatta International airport have arrested two Singaporeans for smuggling 70,431 Ecstasy pills worth an estimated $1.8 million, the Jakarta Post said on Tuesday.

The paper quoted Thomas Sugijata, director of prevention and investigation at customs, as saying the two were arrested on Sunday evening after they arrived in Jakarta on a flight from Paris via Hong Kong.
He said the pills, which had an estimated street value of 4.2 billion rupiah ($1.8 million), were packed in three plastic bags kept in children's toy boxes.
"Some of the pills were mixed with peppermint," he said, adding that others were covered with carbon paper. The pills were found when the suspects' luggage was X-rayed.

"This is the largest haul we've ever made, so far, after the seizure of 60,000 Ecstasy pills in the airport in April," Sugijata said, referring to a case where the pills had been left in unclaimed baggage.

The newspaper said the suspects, identified as a 41-year-old businessman and 28-year-old contractor, were members of a drug syndicate and had disclosed during interrogation that they were working for a group that operated out of discotheques in the region.
Sugijata said customs had seized 239,048 Ecstasy pills since March this year.
Ecstasy has gained wide popularity in Indonesian cities in recent years. Numerous high-profile arrests have led to calls for stricter controls on the drug.
